items.about: greeting that matches the time of day
q: がっこうで　あさ、せんせいに　＿＿＿と　いいます。
がっこうで　あさ、せんせいに　＿＿＿と　いいます。
Gakkō de asa, sensei ni ___ to iimasu.
At school in the morning, you say ___ to your teacher.
items.why: おはようございます is the morning greeting that fits before lunch; こんにちは is correct in meaning but the wrong time of day, and さようなら is for leaving, not arriving.

items.about: です frame for stating your name
q: わたしの　なまえは　ミア＿＿＿。
わたしの　なまえは　ミア＿＿＿。
Watashi no namae wa Mia ___.
My name ___ Mia. (choose the ending)
items.why: です correctly states the fact in the present; でした wrongly claims this was true in the past, and ですか turns the statement into a question rather than an introduction.

q: わたしは　じゅうに＿＿＿です。
わたしは　じゅうに＿＿＿です。
Watashi wa jūni___ desu.
I am twelve ___. (choose the counter)
items.why: さい is the counter for age; にん counts people themselves rather than years, and ひき counts small animals, so さい is the only counter that fits how old you are.

items.about: kana shape: め vs ぬ
q: 「あめ」の　さいごの　じは　どれですか。
「あめ」の　さいごの　じは　どれですか。
Ame no saigo no ji wa dore desu ka.
Which character is the last letter in ame (rain)?
items.why: め is the correct match, a single stroke curling into a small loop; ぬ looks similar but adds an extra loop making a different sound, and わ has an unrelated shape and is a common third guess.

items.about: topic は read as わ
q: 「わたしは　がくせいです」の　「は」は、なんと　よみますか。
「わたしは　がくせいです」の　「は」は、なんと　よみますか。
Watashi wa gakusei desu no wa wa, nanto yomimasu ka.
In watashi wa gakusei desu, how do you read the は?
items.why: As the topic particle, は is written は but read わ; picking は (ha) as the reading is the classic beginner mix-up, and ば is an unrelated sound with a dakuten.

items.about: います for a family member being home
q: あねが　いえに　＿＿＿。
あねが　いえに　＿＿＿。
Ane ga ie ni ___.
My older sister ___ at home. (choose the verb)
items.why: います is the existence verb for people and animals; あります is for objects and places, not people, and です is the copula for identifying or describing something, not for saying someone is present.

items.about: も to add a second family member
q: あねが　います。いぬ＿＿＿　います。
あねが　います。いぬ＿＿＿　います。
Ane ga imasu. Inu ___ imasu.
My older sister is here. The dog is, ___.
items.why: も adds the dog to the list started by あねが います, meaning the dog too; は would make the dog a fresh contrasted topic instead, and が would simply restate existence with no sense of also.

q: かぞくは　よ＿＿＿　です。
かぞくは　よ＿＿＿　です。
Kazoku wa yo___ desu.
My family is four ___. (choose the counter)
items.why: にん is the counter for people; ひき counts small animals, not people, and さい counts years of age, not headcount.

q: 「good morning」は日本語で何ですか。
「good morning」は　にほんごで　なんですか。
'good morning' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'good morning'?
items.why: おはよう is the greeting used specifically in the morning; こんにちは is a real greeting but for after lunch, and さようなら is for leaving, not arriving.

q: 「thank you」は日本語で何ですか。
「thank you」は　にほんごで　なんですか。
'thank you' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'thank you'?
items.why: ありがとう is the set phrase for thanking someone; すみません is for apologising or getting attention, a different social function, and なまえ is an unrelated noun meaning name.

items.about: すき as a です sentence, not a verb
q: わたしは　テニスが　＿＿＿。
わたしは　テニスが　＿＿＿。
Watashi wa tenisu ga ___.
I like tennis. (choose the ending)
items.why: すきです is the correct です-sentence pattern for liking something; すきします wrongly treats すき like an action verb needing します, and すきだ keeps the same meaning but drops the polite register expected here.

items.about: が for the thing being liked
q: すし＿＿＿　すきです。
すし＿＿＿　すきです。
Sushi ___ suki desu.
I like sushi. (choose the particle)
items.why: が marks the thing being liked in すき sentences; は would turn すし into a contrasted topic instead, an odd way to open, and を is for objects of action verbs, which すき does not take.

items.about: か to turn a statement into a question
q: すきです＿＿＿。
すきです＿＿＿。
Suki desu ___.
Do you like it? (choose the ending that asks)
items.why: か turns the statement into a genuine yes or no question; ね checks agreement assuming you already share the feeling, not a real question, and よ adds emphasis or news, also not a question marker.

q: 「older brother」は日本語で何ですか。
「older brother」は　にほんごで　なんですか。
'older brother' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'older brother'?
items.why: あに is the word for an older brother, used when speaking about your own family to others; あね is the equivalent for an older sister, and おとうと means younger brother, the wrong direction of age.

q: 「cat」は日本語で何ですか。
「cat」は　にほんごで　なんですか。
'cat' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'cat'?
items.why: ねこ specifically means cat; いぬ means dog, the classic paired mix-up, and どうぶつ is the general word for animal, too broad to mean cat specifically.

q: じゅぎょうは　く＿＿＿に　はじまります。
じゅぎょうは　く＿＿＿に　はじまります。
Jugyō wa ku___ ni hajimarimasu.
The lesson starts at nine ___. (choose the counter)
items.why: じ is the counter for the hour on a clock; にん counts people, and さい counts years of age, neither of which fits a clock time.

items.about: に marks the point in time
q: くじ＿＿＿　はじまります。
くじ＿＿＿　はじまります。
Kuji ___ hajimarimasu.
It starts at nine o'clock. (choose the particle)
items.why: に marks the point in time an event happens; で marks the place where an action occurs, not a time, and を marks a direct object, but there is nothing being acted on here.

items.about: ます for a regular routine
q: まいにち　べんきょう　＿＿＿。
まいにち　べんきょう　＿＿＿。
Mainichi benkyō ___.
I study every day. (choose the ending)
items.why: します is the polite present habitual form, right for describing a regular routine; した is the plain past form, wrongly claiming it already finished, and する is plain present, correct in meaning but the wrong politeness register here.

q: 「movie」は日本語で何ですか。
「movie」は　にほんごで　なんですか。
'movie' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'movie'?
items.why: えいが means movie; まんが is the visually similar but different word for comic, a classic mix-up, and うんどう means exercise, unrelated in meaning.

q: 「vegetable」は日本語で何ですか。
「vegetable」は　にほんごで　なんですか。
'vegetable' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'vegetable'?
items.why: やさい specifically means vegetable; くだもの means fruit, the natural paired opposite, and たべもの is the broad word for food in general, too wide to mean vegetable specifically.

items.about: ます for a daily routine
q: 毎日、七時に　おき＿＿＿。
まいにち、しちじに　おき＿＿＿。
Mainichi, shichiji ni oki___.
I get up at seven o'clock every day. (choose the ending)
items.why: ます is the polite present habitual ending, right for something that happens every day; ました wrongly puts it in the past, as if it no longer happens, and る is the plain dictionary form, not the polite register expected here.

q: 七時＿＿＿　おきます。
しちじ＿＿＿　おきます。
Shichiji ___ okimasu.
I get up at seven o'clock. (choose the particle)
items.why: に nails a clock time to the event described; を would mark a direct object, not a time, and で marks where an action happens, not when it happens.

q: 「食べます」の　もとの　ぶぶんは　＿＿＿です。
「たべます」の　もとの　ぶぶんは　＿＿＿です。
Tabemasu no moto no bubun wa ___ desu.
The stem of tabemasu (to eat) is ___.
items.why: たべ is what remains once ます is removed, the working stem everything else builds on; たべる is the full plain dictionary form, not the stem, and たべます is the whole polite verb, not just its stem.

q: 「maths」は日本語で何ですか。
「maths」は　にほんごで　なんですか。
'maths' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'maths'?
items.why: すうがく means maths; えいご means English, a different subject entirely, and たいいく means PE, also a different subject.

q: 「Monday」は日本語で何ですか。
「Monday」は　にほんごで　なんですか。
'Monday' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'Monday'?
items.why: げつようび specifically names Monday; ようび is only the generic ending meaning day of the week, not a day itself, and じかん means time or hours, unrelated to naming a day.

items.about: て-form plus ください to request
q: メニューを　見＿＿＿　ください。
メニューを　み＿＿＿　ください。
Menyū o mi___ kudasai.
Please show me the menu. (choose the ending)
items.why: て-form plus ください is the polite request pattern; ます is the plain polite ending, not the connecting form ください needs, and る is the plain dictionary ending, also not the right form to attach ください to.

q: これは　三百＿＿＿です。
これは　さんびゃく＿＿＿です。
Kore wa sanbyaku ___ desu.
This is three hundred yen. (choose the counter)
items.why: えん is the counter for Japanese currency; じ counts the hour on a clock, and にん counts people, neither of which fits a price.

q: ＿＿＿　食べたいです。
＿＿＿　たべたいです。
___ tabetai desu.
I want to eat more.
items.why: もっと specifically means more, matching the intended meaning; ちょっと means a little, the opposite direction of amount, and たくさん means a lot, a large fixed quantity rather than a comparative more.

q: 「breakfast」は日本語で何ですか。
「breakfast」は　にほんごで　なんですか。
'breakfast' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'breakfast'?
items.why: あさごはん means breakfast; ばんごはん means dinner, the paired meal eaten later in the day, and せいかつ means daily life or routine as a whole, not a specific meal.

q: 「homework」は日本語で何ですか。
「homework」は　にほんごで　なんですか。
'homework' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'homework'?
items.why: しゅくだい means homework; テレビ means television, an unrelated noun, and じかん means time, also unrelated to a set task.

items.about: ませんか to invite someone
q: 一緒に　テニスを　し＿＿＿。
いっしょに　テニスを　し＿＿＿。
Issho ni tenisu o shi___.
Would you like to play tennis together? (choose the ending)
items.why: ませんか is the standard soft-invitation ending, meaning won't you play together; ますか merely asks whether the action happens at all, not an invitation, and ましたか wrongly asks about the past, as if checking whether it already happened.

q: 公園＿＿＿　テニスを　します。
こうえん＿＿＿　テニスを　します。
Kōen ___ tenisu o shimasu.
I play tennis at the park. (choose the particle)
items.why: で marks the place where an action happens, right for at the park; に would suggest a destination or a fixed time rather than the location of the activity, and を is reserved for the thing being played, テニスを, not the place.

q: 上手です＿＿＿。
じょうずです＿＿＿。
Jōzu desu ___.
You're good at it, aren't you. (choose the ending)
items.why: ね seeks agreement, matching aren't you in English; か would turn it into a genuine yes or no question instead of a comment, and よ shares new information the listener did not already know, a different function from checking agreement.

q: 「expensive」は日本語で何ですか。
「expensive」は　にほんごで　なんですか。
'expensive' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'expensive'?
items.why: たかい means expensive, or tall; やすい is its opposite, meaning cheap, the classic paired mix-up, and おいしい means delicious, an unrelated quality.

q: 「restaurant」は日本語で何ですか。
「restaurant」は　にほんごで　なんですか。
'restaurant' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'restaurant'?
items.why: レストラン means restaurant; メニュー means menu, a related but different noun found inside a restaurant, and かいもの means shopping, a different activity altogether.

q: 図書館＿＿＿　いきます。
としょかん＿＿＿　いきます。
Toshokan ___ ikimasu.
I go to the library. (choose the particle)
items.why: へ points toward a destination, right for go to the library; で marks where an action takes place, not a direction of movement, and を marks a direct object, but いきます, a motion verb, does not take one.

items.about: ました for a completed weekend trip
q: どこに　行き＿＿＿か。
どこに　いき＿＿＿か。
Doko ni iki___ ka.
Where did you go? (choose the ending)
items.why: ました is the polite past ending, right for asking about a completed weekend trip; ます is present or habitual, wrongly implying it happens regularly rather than once already, and ましょう is a let's suggestion, not a question about the past.

items.about: それから to sequence two actions
q: 図書館に　行きました。＿＿＿、店で　買い物を　しました。
としょかんに　いきました。＿＿＿、みせで　かいものを　しました。
Toshokan ni ikimashita. ___, mise de kaimono o shimashita.
I went to the library. ___, I did some shopping at a shop.
items.why: それから chains one finished action onto the next in sequence, meaning after that; でも means but, wrongly implying a contrast between the two actions, and だから means so or therefore, wrongly implying the shopping was a result caused by the library trip.

q: 「hobby」は日本語で何ですか。
「hobby」は　にほんごで　なんですか。
'hobby' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'hobby'?
items.why: しゅみ means hobby; れんしゅう means practice, a related but different activity, and うた means song, an unrelated noun.

q: 「Saturday」は日本語で何ですか。
「Saturday」は　にほんごで　なんですか。
'Saturday' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'Saturday'?
items.why: どようび means Saturday; こうえん means park, an unrelated place word, and たのしい means fun, an adjective rather than a day name.

items.about: て-form request: あける → あけて
q: 窓を＿＿＿ください。
まどを＿＿＿ください。
Mado o ___ kudasai.
Please ___ the window.
items.why: あけて is the て-form that ください needs to make a polite request; あけます is a plain polite statement with no request meaning, and あけない is a negative form that cannot attach to ください at all.

items.about: から・まで: marking the route
q: 駅＿＿＿学校まで歩きます。
えき＿＿＿がっこうまであるきます。
Eki ___ gakkō made arukimasu.
I walk ___ the station to school.
items.why: から marks the starting point of the route, pairing with まで at the other end; まで cannot mark a starting point since it is already doing that job at school, and を would mark a road walked along, not the point you set off from.

q: 「出口」の意味は何ですか。
「でぐち」のいみはなんですか。
'Deguchi' no imi wa nan desu ka.
What does the sign '出口' mean?
items.why: 出口 combines out and mouth to mean exit, the sign you look for on your way out; entrance uses a different sign, 入口, and platform is not what this particular sign marks.

q: 「library」は日本語で何ですか。
「library」はにほんごでなんですか。
'library' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'library'?
items.why: としょかん means library, the building for borrowing books; えいがかん is the cinema, a completely different building, and えき is the train station, not a place to borrow books.

q: 「taxi」は日本語で何ですか。
「taxi」はにほんごでなんですか。
'taxi' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'taxi'?
items.why: タクシー is a loanword for taxi; バス means bus and でんしゃ means train, both different kinds of transport from a taxi.

q: 水を＿＿＿飲みます。
みずを＿＿＿のみます。
Mizu o ___ nomimasu.
I drink a lot of water.
items.why: たくさん means a lot, matching drinking plenty of water; ちょっと means only a little, the opposite amount, and もっと means more, comparing to an earlier amount rather than naming a lot on its own.

items.about: て-form chain: きって、たべます
q: 野菜を＿＿＿、食べます。
やさいを＿＿＿、たべます。
Yasai o ___, tabemasu.
I cut the vegetables, and eat them.
items.why: きって is the て-form that links cutting to the next action, eating; きります is a plain, full-stop form that cannot chain into the next verb this way, and きらない is negative, wrongly saying you do not cut the vegetables at all.

items.about: school lunch word: きゅうしょく
q: 「lunch」は日本語で何ですか。
「lunch」はにほんごでなんですか。
'Lunch' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'lunch' at school?
items.why: きゅうしょく specifically means school lunch, the meal served at school; ばんごはん means dinner and あさごはん means breakfast, both eaten at home rather than at school.

q: 「bridge」は日本語で何ですか。
「bridge」はにほんごでなんですか。
'bridge' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'bridge'?
items.why: 橋 means bridge, a structure that crosses a river or road; 道 means road or path and 駅 means station, neither of which describes a crossing structure.

q: 「right (the direction)」は日本語で何ですか。
「right (the direction)」はにほんごでなんですか。
'right (the direction)' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'right (the direction)'?
items.why: 右 means right, the direction; 左 means left, the opposite direction, and 店 means shop, unrelated to direction.

q: 暑い＿＿＿、泳ぎます。
あつい＿＿＿、およぎます。
Atsui ___, oyogimasu.
Because it's hot, I swim.
items.why: から attaches to the reason clause to explain why you swim, matching because it's hot; でも means but and starts a contrast instead of a reason, and し simply lists one fact among others without giving a cause.

items.about: いちばん: naming a favourite
q: 夏が＿＿＿好きです。
なつが＿＿＿すきです。
Natsu ga ___ suki desu.
Summer is my favourite.
items.why: いちばん marks summer as the top choice, your favourite; もっと means more, comparing to something else rather than naming a single favourite, and ちょっと means a little, which does not fit a strong preference.

q: 昨日、映画を＿＿＿。
きのう、えいがを＿＿＿。
Kinō, eiga o ___.
Yesterday, I watched a movie.
items.why: みました is the polite past tense that matches きのう, yesterday; みます is present tense so it does not fit a completed past action, and みません is a negative, wrongly saying you did not watch it.

q: 「vegetables」は日本語で何ですか。
「vegetables」はにほんごでなんですか。
'vegetables' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'vegetables'?
items.why: 野菜 means vegetables; 味 means taste or flavour and 料理 means a cooked dish, neither of which names the vegetables themselves.

q: 「spicy」は日本語で何ですか。
「spicy」はにほんごでなんですか。
'spicy' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'spicy'?
items.why: 辛い means spicy, the burning taste from chilli; 健康 means health and 運動 means exercise, both unrelated to taste.

items.about: plain form with a friend: たべる
q: ともだち:「これ、＿＿＿？」
Tomodachi: 'Kore, ___?'
Friend: 'Do you eat this?'
items.why: たべる is the plain, casual form friends use with each other; たべます is the polite form used with teachers or strangers, too formal for a friend's question, and たべました wrongly shifts the question into the past.

items.about: でも: pushing back with a contrast
q: 楽しいです。＿＿＿、難しいです。
たのしいです。＿＿＿、むずかしいです。
Tanoshii desu. ___, muzukashii desu.
It's fun. But, it's difficult.
items.why: でも starts a new sentence to push back with a contrast, fun but also difficult; それから means after that, adding a next step rather than a contrast, and だから means so, wrongly presenting difficulty as a result of being fun.

items.about: reading a short notice: 休み
q: 「明日は休みです。」これは何を言っていますか。
「あしたはやすみです。」これはなにをいっていますか。
'Ashita wa yasumi desu.' Kore wa nani o itte imasu ka.
'Tomorrow is a day off.' What does this say?
items.why: 休み means a day off, so the notice announces there is no school tomorrow; the other two options both describe school happening, the opposite of what 休み says.

q: 「typhoon」は日本語で何ですか。
「typhoon」はにほんごでなんですか。
'typhoon' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'typhoon'?
items.why: 台風 means typhoon, a storm strong enough to close schools; 天気 just means weather in general and 雲 means cloud, neither naming the storm itself.

q: 「fireworks」は日本語で何ですか。
「fireworks」はにほんごでなんですか。
'fireworks' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'fireworks'?
items.why: 花火 means fireworks, the bursts of light watched at summer festivals; 花見 means flower viewing in spring and もみじ means the autumn leaves, both different seasonal customs.

q: 十五歳＿＿＿、オーストラリア人です。
じゅうごさい＿＿＿、オーストラリアじんです。
Jūgo-sai ___, Ōsutoraria-jin desu.
I'm fifteen, and I'm Australian.
items.why: で links two facts about yourself into one sentence, your age and nationality; が would mark a subject doing something rather than chain the two facts together, and を marks a direct object, which fits neither noun here.

items.about: plain form + こと: 泳ぐことが好き
q: 泳ぐ＿＿＿が好きです。
およぐ＿＿＿がすきです。
Oyogu ___ ga suki desu.
I like swimming.
items.why: こと turns the plain verb およぐ into a noun that が can attach to, naming the act of swimming as the thing you like; とき means when or time and does not turn a verb into something likeable, and もの refers to a physical object, not an activity.

q: 楽しいです＿＿＿。
たのしいです＿＿＿。
Tanoshii desu ___.
It's fun, isn't it.
items.why: ね invites agreement, matching isn't it; か would turn the sentence into a plain question instead of a shared observation, and を is an object particle that cannot end a sentence like this at all.

q: 「homework」は日本語で何ですか。
「homework」はにほんごでなんですか。
'homework' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'homework'?
items.why: 宿題 means homework, work assigned to finish outside class; 試験 means an exam and 授業 means a lesson period, both different school concepts.

q: 「teacher」は日本語で何ですか。
「teacher」はにほんごでなんですか。
'teacher' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'teacher'?
items.why: 先生 means teacher, the adult who teaches the class; 生徒 means student and 教室 means classroom, neither naming the person at the front of the room.

items.about: てから: after doing one thing first
q: 宿題を＿＿＿、遊びます。
しゅくだいを＿＿＿、あそびます。
Shukudai o ___, asobimasu.
After I finish my homework, I play.
items.why: してから fixes the order, homework first, then playing; します is a plain present-tense verb that cannot chain into the next clause this way, and しない is negative, wrongly saying you don't do your homework at all.

q: 雨が＿＿＿、家にいます。
あめが＿＿＿、うちにいます。
Ame ga ___, uchi ni imasu.
If it rains, I'll stay home.
items.why: ふったら sets up the if-clause, only if it rains; ふります is a plain future statement with no if-condition attached, and ふりません wrongly negates the rain instead of conditioning your plan on it.

items.about: stem + に行く: going to swim
q: プールへ＿＿＿行きます。
プールへ＿＿＿いきます。
Pūru e ___ ikimasu.
I'm going to the pool to swim.
items.why: およぎに uses the verb stem before に行く to state the purpose of going, to swim; およいで is the て-form, used for chaining actions rather than stating a purpose, and およぎます is the full polite form, which cannot slot in directly before 行きます like this.

q: 「personality」は日本語で何ですか。
「personality」はにほんごでなんですか。
'personality' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'personality'?
items.why: 性格 means personality, the kind of person someone is; 得意 means something you're good at and 趣味 means a hobby, neither describing character itself.

q: 「hometown or where youre from」は日本語で何ですか。
「hometown or where youre from」はにほんごでなんですか。
'hometown or where youre from' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'hometown or where youre from'?
items.why: 出身 means hometown or where you're originally from; 特技 means a special skill and 電話 means telephone, both unrelated to where someone is from.

items.about: そうです: reporting what you heard
q: 新しい映画が＿＿＿そうです。
あたらしいえいがが＿＿＿そうです。
Atarashii eiga ga ___ sō desu.
I heard a new movie is starting.
items.why: はじまる is the plain form that hearsay そうです attaches to, saying you heard it starts; はじまります is the polite form, which cannot sit directly before そうです; はじまり is the bare stem, which attaches to nothing here.

items.about: のが好き: liking an activity
q: 歌を聞く＿＿＿好きです。
うたをきく＿＿＿すきです。
Uta o kiku ___ suki desu.
I like listening to songs.
items.why: のが turns listening into a noun that が can attach to, for liking the whole activity; をが stacks two particles together, which is never grammatical, and には does not fit this pattern, it marks emphasis on a location or topic instead.

items.about: より…ほうが: comparing two things
q: 映画＿＿＿本のほうが面白いです。
えいが＿＿＿ほんのほうがおもしろいです。
Eiga ___ hon no hō ga omoshiroi desu.
The book is more interesting than the movie.
items.why: より marks the movie as the thing being outranked, with ほうが on the winning side, the book; が would mark the movie as a subject rather than the losing side of a comparison, and で marks a place or method, neither of which fits a comparison.

q: 「luggage」は日本語で何ですか。
「luggage」はにほんごでなんですか。
'luggage' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'luggage'?
items.why: 荷物 means luggage, the bags a traveller carries; かばん means a bag in general and 買い物 means shopping, neither naming a traveller's luggage specifically.

q: 「booking or reservation」は日本語で何ですか。
「booking or reservation」はにほんごでなんですか。
'booking or reservation' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'booking or reservation'?
items.why: 予約 means a booking or reservation, arranged in advance; 出発 means departure and 計画 means a plan, both related to travel but not the act of reserving something.

items.about: ことができる: stating a skill
q: 日本語を話す＿＿＿ができます。
にほんごをはなす＿＿＿ができます。
Nihongo o hanasu ___ ga dekimasu.
I'm able to speak Japanese.
items.why: こと turns the plain verb はなす into a noun that ができる can attach to, naming the skill itself; とき means when and もの means a physical thing, neither of which turns a verb into something you can be able to do.

q: 卒業＿＿＿、働きます。
そつぎょう＿＿＿、はたらきます。
Sotsugyō ___, hatarakimasu.
After I graduate, I'll work.
items.why: したら hangs the plan on finishing school first, only after that; します is a plain present statement with no conditional link, and しません wrongly negates graduating altogether.

items.about: なければ: what you have to do
q: 早く起き＿＿＿なりません。
はやくおき＿＿＿なりません。
Hayaku oki ___ narimasen.
I have to get up early.
items.why: なければ pairs with なりません to state a real requirement, you must get up early; ながら means while doing something else at the same time, and たら sets up a mere if-condition rather than a firm obligation.

q: 「popularity」は日本語で何ですか。
「popularity」はにほんごでなんですか。
'popularity' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'popularity'?
items.why: 人気 means popularity, how much something is liked; 感想 means your thoughts or impressions and 内容 means the content of something, neither describing how well liked it is.

q: 「singer」は日本語で何ですか。
「singer」はにほんごでなんですか。
'singer' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'singer'?
items.why: 歌手 means singer, a person whose job is singing; 歌 means song, the thing they sing, and 雑誌 means magazine, unrelated to performing.

q: 朝ご飯を＿＿＿、学校へ行きます。
あさごはんを＿＿＿、がっこうへいきます。
Asagohan o ___, gakkō e ikimasu.
I eat breakfast, and then go to school. (Choose the word for the blank.)
items.why: 食べて, the て-form, links eating breakfast to going to school as the next step; 食べます would end the sentence right there instead of continuing on; 食べる is the plain dictionary form, which cannot chain into another clause this way.

q: きょう、すしを＿＿＿。
きょう、すしを＿＿＿。
Kyō, sushi o ___.
Today, I want to eat sushi. (Choose the word for the blank.)
items.why: 食べたいです, stem+たい, expresses wanting to eat; 食べます simply reports doing it as a fact, not a wish; 食べました wrongly puts it in the past, when the sentence is about today.

q: わたしはパン＿すきです。
わたしはパン＿すきです。
Watashi wa pan ___ suki desu.
I like bread. (Choose the correct particle for the blank.)
items.why: すき always takes が for the thing being liked; を marks the object of an action verb, which すき is not; は would double up the topic marker in the same clause, which does not fit here.

q: 「the meal you eat soon after waking up, before school」は日本語で何ですか。
「the meal you eat soon after waking up, before school」はにほんごでなんですか。
'the meal you eat soon after waking up, before school' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'the meal you eat soon after waking up, before school'?
items.why: あさごはん names the morning meal, built from あさ (morning); ばんごはん is the family's evening meal instead; しゅくだい means homework, not a meal.

q: 「the set work a teacher gives you to finish at home after school」は日本語で何ですか。
「the set work a teacher gives you to finish at home after school」はにほんごでなんですか。
'the set work a teacher gives you to finish at home after school' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'the set work a teacher gives you to finish at home after school'?
items.why: しゅくだい is exactly that take-home task; じかん means time or hours, not a task; うんどう means exercise, which is unrelated to schoolwork.

items.about: desu/deshita: past tense for a day name
q: きのうは月ようび＿＿＿。
きのうはげつようび＿＿＿。
Kinō wa getsuyōbi ___.
Yesterday was Monday. (Choose the word for the blank.)
items.why: でした is the polite past of です, correctly saying yesterday WAS Monday; です would wrongly describe yesterday in the present tense; ではありません flips the meaning to a negative, denying it was Monday.

q: わたし＿がくせいです。
わたし＿がくせいです。
Watashi ___ gakusei desu.
I am a student. (Choose the correct particle for the blank.)
items.why: は marks わたし as the topic of the sentence, the basic pattern for a です statement; を marks a direct object, which this sentence does not have; に marks a time or destination, neither of which fits here.

q: つかれました＿＿＿、はやくねます。
つかれました＿＿＿、はやくねます。
Tsukaremashita ___, hayaku nemasu.
I'm tired, so I'll go to sleep early. (Choose the word for the blank.)
items.why: から gives the reason: tired, so going to sleep early; が would only set up a contrast (tired, but...), not a cause; でも means however and cannot join two clauses like this mid-sentence.

q: 「the whole group of people you live with and are related to」は日本語で何ですか。
「the whole group of people you live with and are related to」はにほんごでなんですか。
'the whole group of people you live with and are related to' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'the whole group of people you live with and are related to'?
items.why: かぞく is the general word for one's whole family; きょうだい names siblings specifically, a narrower group; どうぶつ means animal, unrelated to family.

q: 「a common four legged pet known for loyalty, walks and barking」は日本語で何ですか。
「a common four legged pet known for loyalty, walks and barking」はにほんごでなんですか。
'a common four legged pet known for loyalty, walks and barking' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'a common four legged pet known for loyalty, walks and barking'?
items.why: いぬ is the word for dog specifically; ねこ names a cat instead; ペット is the general word for any pet, not this specific animal.

q: 雨が＿＿＿、うちにいます。
あめが＿＿＿、うちにいます。
Ame ga ___, uchi ni imasu.
If it rains, I'll stay home. (Choose the word for the blank.)
items.why: ふったら (verb+たら) sets up the if-condition, if it rains; ふります is a plain statement of fact, not a condition; ふって is the て-form, which would link two actions in sequence rather than posing a condition.

items.about: no nominalising a verb before ga suki
q: 本を読む＿＿好きです。
ほんをよむ＿＿すきです。
Hon o yomu ___ suki desu.
I like reading books. (Choose the word for the blank.)
items.why: の turns 'reading a book' into a noun phrase that が好き can attach to, the pattern for liking a whole activity; を would need the sentence to already have a noun object, which 読む on its own is not; が cannot follow a plain verb directly without の making it a noun first.

q: 天気よほうによると、あした雨が＿＿＿。
てんきよほうによると、あしたあめが＿＿＿。
Tenki yohō ni yoru to, ashita ame ga ___.
According to the weather forecast, it will apparently rain tomorrow. (Choose the word for the blank.)
items.why: ふるそうです, plain form plus そう, reports what the forecast said, hearsay; ふります simply states it will rain as your own claim, with no reporting attached; ふりそうです is the stem+そう form for appearance, 'looks like it', a different pattern about what you can see rather than what you heard.

q: 「the regular tasks a person does to earn money or fulfil a role」は日本語で何ですか。
「the regular tasks a person does to earn money or fulfil a role」はにほんごでなんですか。
'the regular tasks a person does to earn money or fulfil a role' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'the regular tasks a person does to earn money or fulfil a role'?
items.why: 仕事 is the word for one's job or work tasks; 会社 means the company itself, the organisation rather than the tasks; 面接 means a job interview, a single event, not the ongoing work.

q: 「having so much to do that theres barely a spare moment」は日本語で何ですか。
「having so much to do that theres barely a spare moment」はにほんごでなんですか。
'having so much to do that theres barely a spare moment' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'having so much to do that theres barely a spare moment'?
items.why: 忙しい describes being busy with little free time; のんびり means the opposite, relaxed and unhurried; 給料 means salary, an unrelated word about pay, not workload.

q: 日本に＿＿＿ありますか。
にほんに＿＿＿ありますか。
Nihon ni ___ arimasu ka.
Have you ever been to Japan? (Choose the word for the blank.)
items.why: 行ったことが (past plain form + ことがある) asks about experience, whether you've ever been; 行きます is a plain present statement, not a question about experience; 行って is the て-form, which would need to link to another action instead of asking about past experience.

items.about: toki marking a point in time
q: 日本に行った＿＿＿、お寺を見ました。
にほんにいった＿＿＿、おてらをみました。
Nihon ni itta ___, otera o mimashita.
When I went to Japan, I saw a temple. (Choose the word for the blank.)
items.why: とき marks the point in time, when I went to Japan; から would instead give a reason, because I went; ので also gives a reason rather than marking a point in time, so neither fits the meaning here.

q: 夏は冬＿あついです。
なつはふゆ＿あついです。
Natsu wa fuyu ___ atsui desu.
Summer is hotter than winter. (Choose the correct particle for the blank.)
items.why: より marks what is being outranked in a comparison, hotter than winter; だけ means only and does not create a comparison; しか also means only and must pair with a negative verb, which this sentence does not have.

q: 「the season between summer and winter, when leaves change colour」は日本語で何ですか。
「the season between summer and winter, when leaves change colour」はにほんごでなんですか。
'the season between summer and winter, when leaves change colour' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'the season between summer and winter, when leaves change colour'?
items.why: 秋 is the word for autumn, the season of changing leaves; 夏 means summer instead; 冬 means winter, the opposite end of the year.

q: 「bright bursts of colour and sparks set off into the night sky」は日本語で何ですか。
「bright bursts of colour and sparks set off into the night sky」はにほんごでなんですか。
'bright bursts of colour and sparks set off into the night sky' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'bright bursts of colour and sparks set off into the night sky'?
items.why: 花火 names fireworks specifically; 花見 means flower viewing, a different custom entirely; もみじ refers to the red autumn leaves, not fireworks.

q: このえいがを見た＿＿＿ありますか。
このえいがをみた＿＿＿ありますか。
Kono eiga o mita ___ arimasu ka.
Have you ever seen this movie? (Choose the word for the blank.)
items.why: ことが (past plain form + ことがある) asks about experience, whether you've ever seen it; 見ます is a plain present statement, not a question about experience; 見て is the て-form, which would link to another action rather than ask about past experience.

q: 日本語がじょうずになる＿＿＿、まいにちれんしゅうします。
にほんごがじょうずになる＿＿＿、まいにちれんしゅうします。
Nihongo ga jōzu ni naru ___, mainichi renshū shimasu.
In order to get good at Japanese, I practise every day. (Choose the word for the blank.)
items.why: ために shows the purpose behind the action, in order to get good at Japanese; から would instead give a reason for something that already happened, not a goal being aimed at; ので also gives a reason rather than a purpose, so neither matches the meaning here.

q: このえいがはおもしろい＿＿＿思います。
このえいがはおもしろい＿＿＿おもいます。
Kono eiga wa omoshiroi ___ omoimasu.
I think this movie is interesting. (Choose the word for the blank.)
items.why: と marks the end of the quoted opinion right before 思います, I think that X; を would treat the opinion as a direct object, which is not how と思う works; が does not fit this reporting pattern at all.

q: 「a single show or segment broadcast on television, radio or a streaming service」は日本語で何ですか。
「a single show or segment broadcast on television, radio or a streaming service」はにほんごでなんですか。
'a single show or segment broadcast on television, radio or a streaming service' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'a single show or segment broadcast on television, radio or a streaming service'?
items.why: 番組 is the word for a TV or radio programme; 雑誌 means magazine, a printed item instead; 動画 means a video clip, a different kind of media.

q: 「a person whose job is singing, especially as a performer or recording artist」は日本語で何ですか。
「a person whose job is singing, especially as a performer or recording artist」はにほんごでなんですか。
'a person whose job is singing, especially as a performer or recording artist' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'a person whose job is singing, especially as a performer or recording artist'?
items.why: 歌手 names the person who sings professionally; 歌 means the song itself, not the performer; 人気 means popularity, an unrelated concept.

q: テレビを見＿＿＿、ばんごはんを食べます。
テレビをみ＿＿＿、ばんごはんをたべます。
Terebi o mi ___, bangohan o tabemasu.
I eat dinner while watching TV. (Choose the word for the blank.)
items.why: ながら attaches to the verb stem to mean while doing X, matching watching TV at the same time as eating; ました would end the watching as a finished past action instead of an ongoing one; ません negates the verb, which reverses the meaning entirely.

q: ここでしゃしんをとって＿＿＿ですか。
ここでしゃしんをとって＿＿＿ですか。
Koko de shashin o totte ___ desu ka.
Is it OK to take photos here? (Choose the word for the blank.)
items.why: もいい (て-form + もいい) asks for permission, is it OK to do X; はいけない would instead mean must not, the opposite of asking permission; います just continues the verb as an ongoing action, not a request for permission.

q: つくえの上＿本があります。
つくえのうえ＿ほんがあります。
Tsukue no ue ___ hon ga arimasu.
There is a book on the desk. (Choose the correct particle for the blank.)
items.why: に marks the location where something simply exists, matching あります; で marks the place where an action happens, which does not fit あります; を marks a direct object, and this sentence has no action verb to take one.

q: 「to spend the night somewhere away from home, like at a hotel」は日本語で何ですか。
「to spend the night somewhere away from home, like at a hotel」はにほんごでなんですか。
'to spend the night somewhere away from home, like at a hotel' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'to spend the night somewhere away from home, like at a hotel'?
items.why: 泊まる means to stay overnight somewhere; 待つ means to wait, an unrelated action; 出発 means departure, the moment a trip begins, not where you sleep.

q: 「the bags and belongings a traveller carries or checks in for a trip」は日本語で何ですか。
「the bags and belongings a traveller carries or checks in for a trip」はにほんごでなんですか。
'the bags and belongings a traveller carries or checks in for a trip' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'the bags and belongings a traveller carries or checks in for a trip'?
items.why: 荷物 is the word for luggage or baggage; 買い物 means shopping, a different activity; 予約 means a booking or reservation, unrelated to carrying bags.

q: 電車は八時に着く＿＿＿です。
でんしゃははちじにつく＿＿＿です。
Densha wa hachiji ni tsuku ___ desu.
The train should arrive at eight o'clock. (Choose the word for the blank.)
items.why: はず states a confident expectation based on a known schedule, it should arrive at eight; らしい instead signals the speaker is guessing from outside evidence, a softer and less certain claim; そう alone is incomplete here and does not carry the same expected-to meaning as はず.

q: コーラはあまり飲ま＿＿＿いいです。
コーラはあまりのま＿＿＿いいです。
Kōra wa amari noma ___ ii desu.
It's better not to drink much cola. (Choose the word for the blank.)
items.why: ないほうが (nai-form + ほうがいい) gives advice against doing something, better not to drink it; なければ would instead need ならない to state an obligation, a different meaning entirely; なくても pairs with もいい to mean don't have to, not better not to.

q: このみちはあるいて＿いけます。
このみちはあるいて＿いけます。
Kono michi wa aruite ___ ikemasu.
You can only get to this road on foot. (Choose the correct word for the blank.)
items.why: だけ means only and pairs naturally with the affirmative いけます, can only go on foot; しか also means only but must be followed by a negative verb, which いけます is not; より is used for comparison, not for saying only.

q: 「the building where trains stop so passengers can get on and off」は日本語で何ですか。
「the building where trains stop so passengers can get on and off」はにほんごでなんですか。
'the building where trains stop so passengers can get on and off' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'the building where trains stop so passengers can get on and off'?
items.why: えき is the word for train station; みせ means shop, a different kind of building; みち means road or path, not a building at all.

q: 「a large vehicle that drives a set route through town, picking up and dropping off passengers」は日本語で何ですか。
「a large vehicle that drives a set route through town, picking up and dropping off passengers」はにほんごでなんですか。
'a large vehicle that drives a set route through town, picking up and dropping off passengers' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'a large vehicle that drives a set route through town, picking up and dropping off passengers'?
items.why: バス is the word for bus; タクシー means taxi, a hired car instead of a set route; でんしゃ means train, a different vehicle entirely.

items.about: to marking a quote before iimashita
q: 友達は「たのしい」＿＿＿言いました。
ともだちは「たのしい」＿＿＿いいました。
Tomodachi wa 'tanoshii' ___ iimashita.
My friend said, 'It's fun.' (Choose the word for the blank.)
items.why: と marks the quoted words right before 言いました, said that...; を would treat the quote as a direct object, which is not how quoting works in Japanese; が does not fit this reporting pattern at all.

items.about: yo for a confident, telling tone
q: この番組はとてもおもしろいです＿。
このばんぐみはとてもおもしろいです＿。
Kono bangumi wa totemo omoshiroi desu ___.
This show is really interesting, I promise. (Choose the correct word for the blank.)
items.why: よ adds a confident, let me tell you nudge, sharing information the listener does not already have; ね instead seeks agreement, isn't it, which does not match the I promise tone; か would turn the whole sentence into a question, which is not intended here.

items.about: n desu adding an explanatory tone
q: どうしてまいしゅう見ていますか。つづきが気になる＿＿＿。
どうしてまいしゅうみていますか。つづきがきになる＿＿＿。
Dōshite maishū mite imasu ka. Tsuzuki ga ki ni naru ___.
Why do you watch it every week? It's that I'm curious what happens next. (Choose the word for the blank.)
items.why: んです adds an explanatory tone onto the plain form なる, fitting an answer that explains a reason; です alone would sound like a flat, disconnected statement, not an explanation for the question just asked; でした wrongly shifts the explanation into the past, when the curiosity is ongoing.

q: 「a regularly published collection of articles and pictures, printed on glossy paper」は日本語で何ですか。
「a regularly published collection of articles and pictures, printed on glossy paper」はにほんごでなんですか。
'a regularly published collection of articles and pictures, printed on glossy paper' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'a regularly published collection of articles and pictures, printed on glossy paper'?
items.why: 雑誌 is the word for magazine; 記事 means a single article, a smaller piece inside a magazine rather than the whole publication; 動画 means video, a completely different medium.

q: 「how much a person or thing is liked and talked about by a lot of people」は日本語で何ですか。
「how much a person or thing is liked and talked about by a lot of people」はにほんごでなんですか。
'how much a person or thing is liked and talked about by a lot of people' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'how much a person or thing is liked and talked about by a lot of people'?
items.why: 人気 is the word for popularity; 感想 means one's thoughts or impressions after experiencing something, a different idea; 内容 means the content or substance of something, not how popular it is.

items.about: to iu ten de wa: evaluating one aspect
q: けんこう＿＿＿、きゅうしょくはいいと思います。
けんこう＿＿＿、きゅうしょくはいいとおもいます。
Kenkō ___, kyūshoku wa ii to omoimasu.
In terms of health, I think school lunch is good. (Choose the word for the blank.)
items.why: という点では narrows the evaluation to one specific aspect, health, before giving an opinion; によると means according to, which reports a source rather than picking an aspect to evaluate; について simply means about, a more general topic marker that does not signal a focused evaluation.

items.about: koto ni suru vs koto ni naru (own decision)
q: 来年、日本に＿＿＿。
らいねん、にほんに＿＿＿。
Rainen, Nihon ni ___.
I decided to go to Japan next year. (Choose the correct ending for the blank.)
options: 行くことになりました
items.why: 行くことにしました (ことにする) states your own decision to go; 行くことになりました (ことになる) would instead say it was decided for you, by circumstance or someone else, not your own choice; 行くように思います mixes two unrelated patterns and does not mean decided to at all.

items.about: beki for a duty or strong recommendation
q: がくせいはまじめにべんきょうする＿＿＿です。
がくせいはまじめにべんきょうする＿＿＿です。
Gakusei wa majime ni benkyō suru ___ desu.
Students should study seriously. (Choose the word for the blank.)
items.why: べき asserts a duty or strong recommendation, students should study seriously; らしい instead reports something the speaker is guessing based on evidence, not a duty; はず expresses a confident expectation based on known facts, not a moral obligation.

q: 「the adult at school whose job is to teach a subject and who knows your name」は日本語で何ですか。
「the adult at school whose job is to teach a subject and who knows your name」はにほんごでなんですか。
'the adult at school whose job is to teach a subject and who knows your name' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'the adult at school whose job is to teach a subject and who knows your name'?
items.why: 先生 is the word for teacher; 生徒 means student, the opposite role; 部活 means an after-school club activity, not a person.

q: 「a set task used to check what you have learned, with a result at the end」は日本語で何ですか。
「a set task used to check what you have learned, with a result at the end」はにほんごでなんですか。
'a set task used to check what you have learned, with a result at the end' wa nihongo de nan desu ka.
Which word means 'a set task used to check what you have learned, with a result at the end'?
items.why: 試験 is the word for an exam; 宿題 means homework, work done at home rather than a formal test; 授業 means a lesson or class period, not an assessment.
